turns.learner: Hello teacher! I want to practise talking about things around me, like in my room.
turns.tutor:
Hello! Good plan. Let us practise a, an and the.

We use a or an the first time. We use the the second time.
Example: I see a dog in the garden. The dog is happy.

Your turn. Write the second sentence with a or the:
I have an apple. ___ apple is red.

turns.learner: A apple is red. I think a is okay for both, no?
turns.tutor:
You have most of it; let us sharpen one part. A is right for the first time. It is not right for the second time. For the second time we use the same thing again, so we say the.

Example: I have a dog. The dog is brown.

Write the second sentence:
I see a garden. ___ garden is big.

turns.learner: A garden is big. Why not a? It is a garden, no?
turns.tutor:
A is right for a new thing. It is not right when we talk about the same thing again.

Look at the first sentence: I see a garden.
Now look at the second sentence: ___ garden is big.

Is the second garden new or the same? Write one word.

turns.learner: Same. But I still think a garden, because it is a garden.
turns.tutor:
Same is right. Your idea is true for the first garden. It is not true for the same garden the second time.

Look at the blank again. The garden is the same one from the first sentence.

Try again: I see a garden. ___ garden is big.

turns.learner: The garden is big? Maybe the. But I am not sure why not a.
turns.tutor:
Yes, the is right. It is the same garden from the first sentence, so we say the.

Now a new one.
Write a or an: I see ___ ant on the table.

Now write one new example of your own.

turns.learner: I see a ant on the table.
turns.tutor:
You have most of it; let us sharpen one part. The choice between a and an depends on the first sound of the next word, not the spelling.

Say the word after the blank in your head. Listen to its first sound.

Try again: I see ___ ant on the table.
